solution_principle:
3- Paneling Tools: Another powerful Plugin to generate panels.

- First step is to create a rectangular grid using one of the tools in "Grid" tab.  Some of these components take a list of points, which you can generate using GH standard components, or divide a curve using one of the tools under "Curve" tab of PanelingTools.

- Once a grid is created, you can shuffle it using one of the attraction methods under "Grid Attractors" tab.  One output is the shuffled grid, another output is the normalized weights based on the attraction method that can be used for variable offset or variable paneling for example.

- "Grid Utility" tab helps you do things like extracting points from the grid, replace points, extract center grid, expand grids, create surface from grid, etc.

- "Panel Utility" tab has components to pull panel edges to a surface using pull, iso curves or shortest path.

- "Panel2D" tab has many ways to panel the rectangular grid and populate 2D components.

- "Panel3D" contain components to populate 3D patterns between 2 bounding grids.

Source:
http://www.grasshopper3d.com/group/panelingtools

https://wiki.mcneel.com/_media/labs/panelingtools4grasshopperprimer.pdf

3- Paneling Tools: Another powerful Plugin to generate panels.

- Use the "Planar Grid" to generate a planar grid of points.

- Notice the "Gd" OUTPUT of this component, it means a "Grid".

- Let us use the "Point Attraction" component:
- Needs a Point: Build a new Point in Rhino, reference it in Grasshopper and feed it to the Point Attraction's A INPUT.
- Use a Number Slider to play with the magnitude M INPUT.
- Use the "Generate Borders" component to generate lines between points.
- Use the "Generate Faces" component to generate surfaces between points.

- Use the "Morph 2D" component to morph curves inro grid cells:
- Build a circle and feed it to the PC INPUT of the "Morph 2D".

sub_annotations.text:
- Surface Division:

Build a new surface in Rhino, reference it in Grasshopper and try divide it by:

- Either by domain number: Use the "Surface Domain Number" component.
- Or by domain length: Use the "Surface Domain Length" component.
- Or by distance: Use the "Surface Distance" component.
